subtitle: The Akposo harvest thanksgiving
answer: Ovazu is the main harvest festival of the Akposo people of the Biakoye District in the Oti Region. It gives thanks for the fonio crop, called ova, to Uwolowu, the Almighty God, and to the seven principal Akposo gods. It is held at the harvest, between October and December.

sections.title: What it is
sections.html:
Ovazu gives thanks for the fonio harvest, a small grain the Akposo call ova, to Uwolowu (Ayanuva), the Almighty God, and to the seven principal Akposo gods, the greatest of them Wetu.[[1]] It is kept in Akposokubi, Akposo Kabo, Oklabe, Alifi, Obeve (Asukawkaw), Okanease and Akloklowa.[[1]]

The Akposo also keep a yam festival by clan and family, and smaller festivals for lesser gods; each of the seven gods has its own days of worship.[[1]]

Published accounts of Ovazu are short. If you know the festival, tell us more and we’ll add it.

sections.title: Good to know if you go
tips: Where: the Akposo towns are in the Biakoye District. See the Oti page for places nearby.
Check the dates: the traditional council sets them each year. Local radio and the national press carry the announcement.
Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.
